data.title: USDJPY: Dollar Holds Above ¥159 as Tokyo Inflation Keeps BOJ Hike in Play
data.description:
Key points:
  • Tokyo core inflation reaches 2.9%
  • US yields keep the dollar supported
  • ¥160 puts intervention in focus

Japan’s accelerating core inflation strengthens the case for further tightening, but firm US yields leave the yen struggling to gain ground.

💴 Yen struggles despite hotter inflation

  • The pair traded around ¥159.25–¥159.35 early Friday, with the dollar retaining a modest advantage after Tokyo’s inflation release.
  • The figures supported expectations of another Bank of Japan rate increase, but stopped short of delivering the upside surprise that might have prompted a stronger yen rally.
  • Tokyo core consumer prices rose 2.9% annually in November, accelerating from 2.6% in October to a 16-month high. The reading nevertheless missed the 3% consensus forecast.
  • Japan’s core measure excludes fresh food but includes energy, making that distinction important when assessing the underlying inflation signal. Inflation excluding both fresh food and energy eased to 2.5% from 2.6%.

🏦 Two central banks keep traders guessing

  • The BOJ’s December 17–18 meeting is the next major domestic policy test. An increase remains the most likely move.
  • On the other end, the dollar has substantial support of its own. Markets are almost fully pricing a quarter-point Fed increase in December, while the US 10-year Treasury yield has climbed toward 4.89%.
  • A BOJ hike may offer limited relief if US rate expectations rise alongside it. A more durable yen recovery would become easier if Japanese tightening coincided with easing US yields or a less aggressive Fed outlook.

📊 ¥160 keeps traders on alert

  • The ¥160 area remains the immediate psychological reference above the market. Its proximity keeps intervention concerns relevant, but it is not an automatic trigger for official action.
  • Below the market, ¥159 is the nearest round-number reference. Holding above it would preserve the immediate upward bias; sustained trading underneath would indicate buyers losing momentum.
  • Friday’s shortened US session adds a liquidity complication. The pair enters that stretch caught between supportive dollar yields, Japan’s inflation pressure and the possibility of a sharper official response to yen weakness.

data.title: Swiggy's Instamart to layoff 340 employees amid AI transition, says report
data.description:
Artificial Intelligence and its role in taking over employment opportunities and resulting layoffs are gathering pace at an extensive pace.

SWIGGY LAYOFFS

Swiggy's quick delivery/quick commerce arm, Instamart, is set to fire 340 of its employees. As per a report from Moneycontrol, the company, which has lagged behind its competitors, Zomato's Blinkit and Zepto, among others, is planning to lay off 340 employees in its quick-commerce division as it restructures the business for its next stage of growth amid increased adoption of AI.

The report also pointed out that the move comes as competition intensifies, with Eternal-owned Blinkit, Zepto, Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and other players vying for market share. Swiggy, however, remains well capitalised, with approximately Rs 13,500 crore in cash and cash equivalents.

SAP TO FIRE 10,000

This report of layoffs comes on the same day Bloomberg reported that SAP SE is developing a plan to eliminate at least 10,000 jobs as the German software company reshapes its business for an artificial intelligence transition.

The proposed reductions would affect at least 9% of SAP’s global workforce, though the final figure has yet to be determined.

The restructuring is expected to span several departments, including product and engineering, as well as sales. SAP is also revamping how it develops and markets its products as CEO Christian Klein advances an AI-focused strategy.

SWIGGY Q2 RESULTS 

Swiggy posted a smaller net loss in the September quarter, while revenue rose sharply across its businesses. Both food delivery and quick commerce delivered year-on-year growth.

The company recorded a net loss of ₹922 crore in Q2 FY27, down from ₹1,092 crore in the same quarter a year earlier, a reduction of nearly 16%.

Revenue from operations increased 54.4% year on year to ₹5,561 crore, compared with ₹3,601 crore in the year-ago period. This growth reflects ongoing expansion in Swiggy’s food delivery and quick commerce businesses.

data.title: SAP flags security incident, says no evidence of unauthorized access to customer data
data.description:
SAP "has identified suspicious activity" but found no evidence so far of unauthorized access to its customer business data, the German software firm told Reuters on Friday.

In a statement, SAP said it promptly implemented the necessary measures to protect its customers and preserve the security of its services after identifying the activity.

"Based on our investigation to date, we have found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data," it said.

Spiegel magazine reported on Thursday a cyberattack at the company, citing an internal memo to staff.

data.title: China Industrial Profits Log Robust Growth
data.description:
BEIJING (dpa-AFX) - China's industrial profits increased notably in October driven by higher demand for tech products, data published by the National Bureau of Statistics revealed on Friday.

Industrial profits registered an annual growth of 20.1 percent in October, marking the fastest growth in five months. This compared with a 14.4 percent increase posted in September.

For the January to October period, industrial profits advanced 16.0 percent from the same period last year.

Data showed that profit gains were concentrated in technology-related sectors, while consumer-facing manufacturers and construction companies logged losses during the period.

data.title: JSW Energy accepts bids for 7-year bonds, bankers say
data.description:
India's JSW Energy has accepted bids worth 7.50 billion rupees ($80.87 million) for bonds maturing in seven years, three merchant bankers said on Friday.

The issuer will pay a spread of 27 basis points over India Infrastructure Finance Company's base rate of 7.95%, implying an indicative yield of 8.22%, payable semi-annually.

It had invited coupon bids from bankers and investors on Thursday, the bankers said.

The notes have a staggered redemption, with one-third of the principal due at the end of the fifth year, sixth year and seventh year.

The company did not reply to a Reuters email seeking comment.

data.title: China stocks, yuan rally after Beijing vows stronger market support
data.description:
China's share benchmarks jumped more than 3% and the yuan reversed early losses on Friday, after Premier Li Qiang chaired a State Council meeting that called for a bigger role by "national team" investors to stabilise a falling stock market.

China's benchmark Shanghai Composite Index and the blue-chip CSI300 index soared in afternoon trading, putting them on track for their best session in two years.

China's tech-focused STAR 50 Index surged 12%.

In Beijing's strongest gesture yet to support a stock market that had fallen to 16-month lows, the cabinet said "capital markets were crucial to the broader economy," adding that Central Huijin would enhance its role as a quasi-stabilisation fund to ensure ample liquidity, state media Xinhua reported.

The meeting also called for better policies to encourage long-term funds to invest in the stock market, and for measures to strengthen defences against risks spilling over from overseas markets.

"It's a shot in the arm for markets," said Kenny Ng, a strategist at Everbright Securities International in Hong Kong.

"Sentiment has been downbeat for so long. There hasn't been much good news to trade on. At least now there's something to count on: the national team will come to the rescue if things really turn south."

The CSI Semiconductor Industry Index (.CSI931865)，the STAR Chip Index (.STARCHIP) both shot up more than 16%.

Indices tracking China's AI , cloud computing (.CSI930851) and consumer electronics stocks (.CSI931494) jumped more than 10%.

Everbright's Ng added that the meeting sent a clear signal that regulators do not want to see the market slide further, but cautioned that future market trends would be decided by many other factors including US-China relations, tariffs on trade, and chip supply following tighter US restrictions.

The rally also spread to Hong Kong, where the Hang Seng Index gained 2% while the Hang Seng Tech Index (.HSETCH) jumped 6%.

data.title: India urges states to sign 41 GW of pending clean power contracts
data.description:
India's federal government urged states on Friday to sign more contracts for 41 gigawatts (GW) of clean energy capacity that has no buyers.

States need to identify their power requirements well in advance and sign more battery storage contracts along with clean energy, Shripad Naik, union minister of state for power and new and renewable energy, said at the State Power Ministers Conference in New Delhi.

  • The lack of battery energy storage resulted in states scrambling for power to meet their evening and night demand as the El Nino weather pattern pushed up consumption this year

  • The unexpected surge in demand strained India's power system in September and October despite the country having surplus solar energy, Power Secretary Pankaj Agarwal said at the conference

  • Peak power demand of 271 GW in May was 11.6% higher than a year earlier, Agarwal said

  • "There were days we could barely meet their evening peak demand despite having surplus clean energy during the day," Agarwal said

  • Naik also urged states to speed up payments tied to the acquisition of land for transmission projects, saying slow payments have led to huge delays

  • Insufficient transmission capacity has forced India to curtail renewable power generation, which has wasted clean energy

data.title: Imperial Brands Stock Up On Altria's Confirmation Of Possible Takeover Offer
data.description:
HENRICO COUNTY (dpa-AFX) - Shares of Imperial Brands PLC (IMBBY.PK, IMB.L) climbed around 15 percent on Thursday's London trading after U.S. tobacco major Altria Group, Inc. (MO) confirmed a possible takeover offer for the British peer.

Meanwhile, responding to Altria's statement, Imperial Brands said its Board has not had any discussions with, or received any approach or proposal from, Altria or the third party referenced.

Earlier in the day, Altria Group issued a statement in response to recent press speculation, confirming that it is considering a possible offer for Imperial Brands. Any offer, if made, is likely to be solely in cash.

Altria confirmed that it is also in discussions with a third party regarding its possible acquisition of part of the business of Imperial Brands.

However, the companies have not reached any agreement so far. There can be no certainty that an offer will ultimately be made nor as to the terms on which any offer may be made, it said.

Altria is required to announce a firm intention to make an offer for Imperial Brands by no later than December 24, or that it does not intend to make an offer.

Following the news, Imperial Brands said its Board is clear in its duty of aiming to maximise shareholder value and will consider any proposal, should one be made. The firm also urged shareholders not to take any action at this time.

Imperial Brands added that it has strong confidence in its strategy and trading.

On November 17, Imperial Brands reported a drop in pre-tax income and revenue for fiscal 2026, and said it expects fiscal 2027 adjusted operating profit to grow at a similar level to fiscal 2026, on a constant currency basis, primarily driven by continued profit growth from the company's combustible tobacco business.

While reporting the results, the firm also had announced planned job cuts as part of its transformation strategy, which is estimated to generate cost savings of at least 320 million pounds per annum by 2030.

In fiscal year 2026, the company projects reduction of 2,100 roles globally. Additionally, the Bristol-based company plans for a further reduction of between 2,100 and 2,500 roles by the end of 2030.

In London, Imperial Brands shares closed Thursday's trading at 3,432.00 pence, up 14.85 percent.

In the overnight activity on the NYSE, Altria shares were trading 0.33 percent lower at $76.03, after closing Thursday's regular trading 1.95 percent higher.
